draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Saligao! This Bardez village is home to Mater Dei, one of Goa's first English language schools, which started out as St. Mary's back in 1900.
draft.hungryLine: Saligao is a quiet village, so for more choice head 3 km to Calangute, the former fishing village turned tourist spot.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Mae de Deus Church and St. Anne's Chapel are both about a 7 min walk, and Salmona Chapel is around 16 min away.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Calangute beach is just 3 km away if you want sand and sea.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Back in 2001 Saligao's literacy rate was 82 percent, well above the national average of 59.5 percent.

tips.title: Dress modestly at the churches.
tips.body: Saligao's churches and chapels are working places of worship.

tips.title: Add the Houses of Goa Museum.
tips.body: Architect Gerard da Cunha's museum at Salvador-do-Mundo in Bardez shows how eastern and western building styles blended, and opens Tuesday to Sunday.

story.title: Mae de Deus
story.body: Saligao's Mãe de Deus Parish Church was built in 1873.

story.title: An early English school
story.body: St. Mary's opened at Bairo Alto in 1900 as one of Goa's first English language schools. It was renamed Mater Dei in 1909.

story.title: A well read village
story.body: The 2001 census counted 5,553 people in Saligao, with a literacy rate of 82 percent.

story.title: Between towns
story.body: Saligao sits 10 km from Panjim, 6 km from Mapusa and 3 km from Calangute beach, surrounded by villages like Porvorim, Parra, Candolim and Nagoa.
